# Bones of the human skeleton — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/human-skeleton.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/human-skeleton.ttl`](../decks/human-skeleton.ttl) · **Cards:** 54 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

54 bones and bone groups of the human skeleton, from the skull to the foot. Front: the bone's everyday or anatomical name in English and Swedish; back: its Latin name in Terminologia Anatomica (TA98). Compiled from Wikidata, Svensk MeSH and the U.S. National Cancer Institute's SEER Training Modules, the Latin checked against TA98.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0-1.0. Its content comes from three open sources: Wikidata (CC0: labels, aliases and TA98 IDs), Svensk MeSH (CC0, Karolinska Institutets Universitetsbibliotek: Swedish names and Swedish scope notes; NLM's English MeSH data in the same download, which NLM provides freely with acknowledgement, only identified concepts and confirmed facts) and the SEER Training Modules of the U.S. National Cancer Institute (free of copyright: the list of bones the selection starts from). Terminologia Anatomica (all rights reserved) sets the naming convention of the backs: each Latin back is the TA98 preferred term for the bone's code. That is a single standardised name, a fact rather than protected expression; for 44 cards the same term is also a Wikidata la label or alias, for most of the others it is in another open source, and Ossa metacarpi and Ossa metatarsi rest on TA98 alone (see Method). No definitions, descriptions, lists or selections were taken from TA98. The Swedish and English Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used to verify names and the facts in the back notes; no text or selection was taken from them. The back notes state short facts in plain wording; where a phrase matches a source (e.g. "kroppens minsta ben", "the eight small bones of the wrist") it is a minimal factual statement, not protected expression, and where a note follows a Svensk MeSH scope note ("Mellanfotens fem långa ben") that source is CC0 and cited. Attribution, though not required by CC0, is given in the deck (prov:wasDerivedFrom) and in this report: Karolinska Institutets Bibliotek for the Swedish MeSH translation and the U.S. National Library of Medicine for MeSH, as the Svensk MeSH readme and NLM's terms ask, without implying NLM's endorsement.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks and three review rounds by independent AI reviewers (factual accuracy; language and translation; licensing, attribution and documentation), logged under Quality control with every finding and how it was resolved (round 0 is the authoring agent's own source and machine check). The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert. Every value below was fetched on 2026-10-04; the exact queries and the code run on the downloads are listed under Queries. The raw responses and the authoring scripts were kept only in the authoring session's temporary working directory and are not preserved; rerunning the listed queries reproduces the data, though the live sources may have changed since.
2. Candidate list. The two SEER Training Module pages (U.S. National Cancer Institute, public domain) list the bones of the axial and appendicular skeleton. Their entries (cranial and facial bones, auditory ossicles, hyoid, vertebrae, sacrum, coccyx, sternum, ribs, clavicle, scapula, arm and leg bones, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges, hip bones, tarsals, metatarsals) were the starting list. It was extended with well-known bones and groups below that level: the atlas and axis, the auditory ossicles as a group, the vertebral column and the pelvis, the parts of the hip bone (ilium, ischium, pubis) and individual carpal and tarsal bones.
3. Wikidata. A SPARQL query looked up the Wikidata item of each candidate by English label, requiring a Terminologia Anatomica 98 ID (P1323); items it missed were found with wbsearchentities, choosing the item about the human bone (e.g. Q5283631 human mandible, Q9604 human skull, not the general Q16370 or Q13147). wbgetentities then fetched every item's en, sv and la labels and aliases and its P1323 statements.
4. Latin names (back). For each item, the TA98 entity page for its P1323 code was fetched from the TA98 online edition (ifaa.unifr.ch) and parsed for the Latin preferred term, Latin official synonym, English equivalent and English synonym. The card's Latin text follows TA98's naming: it is the TA98 Latin preferred term for the item's code, so TA98 decides which Latin form is on the back where several exist (Femur rather than Os femoris, Ossa metacarpi rather than Ossa metacarpalia). A single standardised anatomical term is a fact, not protected expression, so TA98 (all rights reserved) is listed as a verification source; no definitions, lists or other text were taken from it. Bracketed numbering in TA98 terms (e.g. "vertebrae cervicales [C I - C VII]", "atlas [C I]") is left out. TA98 prints the terms in lower case online; the cards capitalise the first letter, as the library brief does ("Femur"). Where TA98 gives two Latin terms (femur / os femoris, ossa carpi / ossa carpalia, os ilium / ilium) the preferred one is used. The same term is in Wikidata as a la label or alias for 44 of the 54 cards; for the other ten the Wikidata la label is missing (the skull), a synonym, a region name or malformed (see Quality control), and the term was confirmed in a second open source where one exists (a Wikidata en label or alias, a Wikidata sv alias, or a Svensk MeSH synonym or English entry term). For Ossa metacarpi and Ossa metatarsi no open source consulted has the exact preferred term (they give the TA98 official synonyms ossa metacarpalia and ossa metatarsalia, or the region names Metacarpus and Metatarsus), so these two backs rest on TA98 alone.
5. English names (front). Where English has an everyday name for the bone (thigh bone, kneecap, shinbone, calf bone, heel bone, collarbone, shoulder blade, breastbone, tailbone, backbone, cheekbone, upper jaw, lower jaw, hammer, anvil, stirrup), the front uses it; otherwise the English anatomical name (frontal bone, hip bone, scaphoid bone ...). Every English name is a Wikidata en label or alias except three (stirrup, and the plurals auditory ossicles and carpal bones), and each was cross-checked against the TA98 English equivalent or synonym, MeSH, the SEER list or the English Wikipedia introduction. "Stirrup" is common English vocabulary for the stapes; no open content source consulted lists it (Wikidata has only "stapes bone", Svensk MeSH no English synonym), and it rests on the English Wikipedia (verification). For six bones (humerus, radius, ulna, vomer, talus, pelvis) the established English name is the Latin name itself; these cards are kept for their Swedish names (review round 2 considered "Ankle bone" for the talus and "Upper arm bone" for the humerus and kept the anatomical names; see Quality control). The atlas and axis are given descriptively (first and second cervical vertebra), since their English names are also the Latin ones.
6. Swedish names (front). The Swedish name is the Wikidata sv label or alias when it agrees with the Svensk MeSH 2026 term or synonym (Karolinska Institutets Universitetsbibliotek, CC0), compared case-insensitively. Where the two disagree or one is missing, the name was chosen from the open sources and confirmed in the Swedish Wikipedia (verification): skalle (MeSH), underkäke (MeSH), plogben (MeSH synonym), ärtben (MeSH), sittben (MeSH), första/andra halskotan (MeSH), handlovens båtben (MeSH), fotens båtben (MeSH synonym "Båtben i foten", sv.wikipedia "Fotens båtben"), tårben, hakben, mellanhandsben, fotrotsben and tärningsben (Wikidata), bröstkotor and ländkotor (Svensk MeSH plurals of the Wikidata singulars). Swedish names are written in lower case as common nouns; the three ear ossicles are given in the definite form (hammaren, städet, stigbygeln) as Wikidata, Svensk MeSH for städet and the Swedish Wikipedia name them, since the indefinite forms name tools; the other bones are in the indefinite form as in the brief (lårben), except the atlas and axis, which are named with an ordinal and so take the definite form, as Svensk MeSH and the Swedish Wikipedia do (första halskotan, andra halskotan). Groups are in the plural (halskotor, revben, handlovsben).
7. Back notes. A short note on each card says where the bone is or how it is also called, in plain wording written for the deck. Each fact in a note was checked against a Svensk MeSH scope note (KIB's Swedish, or NLM's English one in the same download) where one states it, against the Swedish or English Wikipedia, or against the SEER count, and the supporting sentence is quoted in the card's evidence (for the notes of the atlas, axis, sacrum, maxilla, mandible, vomer, ethmoid, hyoid, lunate, hamate, femur, metacarpal, tarsal and metatarsal cards these quotes were added in review rounds 1-4). Counts that vary between people or sources (the number of bones in the pelvis, the number of fused coccygeal vertebrae) were left out, and the rib note says "most people". Where the sources disagree on a note's fact (the English Wikipedia puts the metatarsals in the midfoot, its Tarsus article and anatomy teaching put them in the forefoot), the note avoids the disputed term.
8. Cross-check. A script (gen.py, run in the authoring session's temporary working directory and not preserved) built each card's evidence from the saved raw data only: the Wikidata labels and P1323 values, the TA98 fields, the Svensk MeSH terms and synonyms, the SEER list item and the Wikipedia quote, asserting that each quoted text occurs in the saved page. For each card it added Wikidata checks for the P1323 code and for every en, sv and la label or alias that equals the card's text apart from capitalisation, using Wikidata's own spelling; every side that has no such label was logged as a finding in round 0 with how it was resolved. The builder re-runs all checks against live Wikidata. After the review rounds, the added evidence was written by a second script (also not preserved) that asserted every new quote against the saved Svensk MeSH tables and Wikipedia texts in the same way.
9. Uniqueness. Every front is unique in English and in Swedish and every Latin back is unique, so the deck is studied in both directions. Where Swedish uses one name for two bones (båtben for both the scaphoid of the wrist and the navicular of the foot), the fronts are qualified as Svensk MeSH and the Swedish Wikipedia do (handlovens båtben, fotens båtben).

## Selection

54 cards: the bones and bone groups that the SEER Training Module lists of the axial and appendicular skeleton name (except the phalanges and the palatine bone and inferior nasal concha, see below), plus the atlas, axis, auditory ossicles as a group, vertebral column, pelvis, the three parts of the hip bone, four carpal bones (scaphoid, lunate, pisiform, hamate) and four tarsal bones (talus, calcaneus, navicular, cuboid). A bone was included only if it has a TA98 code, a TA98 Latin preferred term, an English name and a Swedish name confirmed in two sources. Left out: the phalanges, because TA98 gives the same Latin term (ossa digitorum, phalanges) for the fingers and the toes, so the back would not identify one card; the palatine bone, because the Swedish "gomben" is in Svensk MeSH only as a synonym of the hard palate, not the bone; the inferior nasal concha (Swedish only in the plural group "näsmusslor" in MeSH, no Wikidata sv label); the capitate, triquetrum, trapezium and trapezoid, whose Swedish names vary between sources (Wikidata gives Latin or "lilla mångkantiga benet", the Swedish Wikipedia "huvudbenet", "pyramidbenet", "trapetsbenet", "trapetslika benet", MeSH Latin); the three cuneiform bones, whose names differ only by medial, intermediate and lateral and which Svensk MeSH has only as the group "Kilformade ben"; the rib cage (TA98 cavea thoracis has no Latin label in Wikidata or Swedish synonym in MeSH to confirm it); and sesamoid bones other than the kneecap and the pisiform, whose number varies between people. Individual ribs, vertebrae by number and the bones' parts (processes, heads, sutures) are out of scope.

## Queries

**Find the Wikidata items of candidate bones by English label, with their TA98 ID (P1323) and en/sv/la labels and aliases (SPARQL at https://query.wikidata.org/sparql)** (Wikidata)

```
SELECT ?item ?en (SAMPLE(?ta0) AS ?ta) (SAMPLE(?sv0) AS ?sv) (SAMPLE(?la0) AS ?la) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?a;separator=" | ") AS ?enAliases) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?b;separator=" | ") AS ?svAliases) WHERE {
  VALUES ?en { "skull"@en "frontal bone"@en "parietal bone"@en "occipital bone"@en "temporal bone"@en "sphenoid bone"@en "ethmoid bone"@en "nasal bone"@en "zygomatic bone"@en "lacrimal bone"@en "maxilla"@en "mandible"@en "vomer"@en "palatine bone"@en "hyoid bone"@en "inferior nasal concha"@en "malleus"@en "incus"@en "stapes"@en "vertebral column"@en "cervical vertebrae"@en "thoracic vertebrae"@en "lumbar vertebrae"@en "sacrum"@en "coccyx"@en "atlas"@en "axis"@en "sternum"@en "rib"@en "clavicle"@en "scapula"@en "humerus"@en "radius"@en "ulna"@en "carpal bones"@en "metacarpal bones"@en "phalanges of the hand"@en "scaphoid bone"@en "lunate bone"@en "triquetral bone"@en "pisiform bone"@en "trapezium"@en "trapezoid bone"@en "capitate bone"@en "hamate bone"@en "hip bone"@en "ilium"@en "ischium"@en "pubis"@en "pelvis"@en "femur"@en "patella"@en "tibia"@en "fibula"@en "tarsus"@en "metatarsal bones"@en "phalanges of the foot"@en "talus"@en "calcaneus"@en "navicular bone"@en "cuboid bone"@en "cuneiform bones"@en "medial cuneiform bone"@en "intermediate cuneiform bone"@en "lateral cuneiform bone"@en "neurocranium"@en "viscerocranium"@en "thoracic cage"@en "manubrium of sternum"@en "xiphoid process"@en "body of sternum"@en "cranium"@en "human skeleton"@en "metacarpal bone"@en "metatarsal bone"@en "carpal bone"@en "tarsal bone"@en "phalanx bone"@en "pubic bone"@en "ischial bone"@en "iliac bone"@en "pelvic girdle"@en "shoulder girdle"@en "auditory ossicle"@en "rib cage"@en "vertebra"@en "middle phalanx"@en "proximal phalanx"@en "distal phalanx"@en }
  ?item rdfs:label ?en ; wdt:P1323 ?ta0 .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv0 FILTER(LANG(?sv0)="sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?la0 FILTER(LANG(?la0)="la") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?a FILTER(LANG(?a)="en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?b FILTER(LANG(?b)="sv") }
} GROUP BY ?item ?en
```

**Download the Svensk MeSH 2026 tables (terms.csv, synonyms.csv, mesh_numbers.csv, swe_scope_notes.csv) and list every descriptor under the MeSH trees A02.835.232 (Bone and Bones) and A09.246.397 (Ear, Middle) with its Swedish term and Swedish synonyms** (Svensk MeSH 2026 (Swedish translation of Medical Subject Headings))

```
https://stingray.kib.ki.se/mesh/2026_export/text_files/Svensk_MeSH_textfiler_april_2026.zip
Unzipped to svmesh/2026/; then this Python (mesh.py) listed the descriptors:
import csv, os, collections
D = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "svmesh", "2026")
def rows(f):
    with open(os.path.join(D, f), encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        return list(csv.reader(fh, delimiter="\t"))[1:]
terms = {r[0]: (r[1], r[2]) for r in rows("terms.csv") if len(r) >= 3}
syn = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows("synonyms.csv"):
    if len(r) >= 2: syn[r[1]].append(r[0])
nums = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in rows("mesh_numbers.csv"):
    if len(r) >= 2: nums[r[1]].append(r[0])
sel = sorted({(n, ui) for ui, ns in nums.items() for n in ns if n.startswith(("A02.835.232", "A09.246.397"))})
for n, ui in sel:
    en, sv = terms.get(ui, ("?", "?"))
    print(f"{n:28} {ui:10} {en:35} | {sv:30} | syn: {'; '.join(syn[ui])}")
D010388 (Pelvis), outside these trees, was looked up by its English heading in terms.csv; that command was not recorded.
```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 61 findings: 25 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 35 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (196 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Source cross-check and Wikidata machine checks (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 54 cards, every side

Every card has evidence from Wikidata (content), the TA98 entity page (verification) and at least one of Svensk MeSH, SEER and the Swedish or English Wikipedia. 191 Wikidata checks (194 after the three added in review round 3, 196 after the two added in round 4): the TA98 ID (P1323) of 53 items and every en, sv and la label or alias that equals the card's text apart from case. The 24 card sides with no such Wikidata label are listed below with how they were resolved; the Latin always follows TA98's preferred term, never a disagreeing Wikidata label. Further discrepancies between the sources, and conventions chosen, follow. Not yet reviewed by a human subject expert.

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 54 cards: Latin backs against the TA98 entity pages, TA98 codes against P1323, the selection against the SEER lists, fronts and back notes

The reviewer fetched the TA98 page of every card and found every Latin back equal to the TA98 Latin preferred term (bracketed numbering left out on purpose), the TA98 codes equal to P1323, the builder's 191 Wikidata checks passing and the selection matching SEER. One error (metatarsals called midfoot bones), two warnings (tarsal note "rear foot"; mandible called the skull's movable bone although the ear ossicles, skull bones in TA98 and SEER, also move) and two wording suggestions (vomer; lunate and hamate rows). All five were verified and fixed.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| metatarsal-bones | English note "The five long bones of the midfoot.": the usual division puts the metatarsals in the forefoot; the midfoot is the navicular, cuboid and cuneiforms. Only the English Wikipedia (Metatarsal bones) says midfoot. | Verified: the English Wikipedia's own Tarsus article puts the cuboid, cuneiforms and navicular in the midfoot, and TeachMeAnatomy (https://teachmeanatomy.info/lower-limb/bones/bones-of-the-foot-tarsals-metatarsals-and-phalanges/, fetched 2026-10-04 to check the reviewer's quote, not used as a source) says "Forefoot – metatarsals and phalanges". Note changed to "The five long bones between the tarsal bones and the toes.", supported by the Svensk MeSH scope notes (sv "Mellanfotens fem långa ben, som bildar leder med fotvristbenen ...", NLM en "articulating with the TARSAL BONES proximally and the PHALANGES OF TOES distally") and sv.wikipedia Mellanfot; the Wikipedia discrepancy is recorded in the card's evidence. The Swedish note (mellanfot = metatarsus) is unchanged. | fixed |
| tarsal-bones | English note "The seven bones of the ankle and rear foot.": only the talus and calcaneus are hindfoot bones; the navicular, cuboid and cuneiforms are midfoot. | Verified against en.wikipedia Tarsus ("made up of the midfoot (cuboid, ... navicular) and hindfoot (talus and calcaneus)"). Note changed to "The seven bones of the hindfoot and midfoot." (rather than the suggested "ankle, heel and midfoot", to follow the source's division); evidence added. Swedish "Fotrotens sju ben." unchanged. | fixed |
| mandible | Note "The movable bone of the skull" / "Skallens rörliga ben" implies it is the only one, but the auditory ossicles count as skull bones (TA98, SEER) and move. | Verified (the deck's own ossicle cards and the SEER axial list count the ossicles under the skull). Note changed to en "Moves at the jaw joint; holds the lower teeth.", sv "Rör sig i käkleden; här sitter de nedre tänderna.", supported by sv.wikipedia Käke ("Underkäken är rörlig medelst en led"), en.wikipedia Mandible ("sharing joints with the cranium's temporal bones", "The mandible hosts the lower teeth") and the Svensk MeSH scope note ("I underkäken sitter den undre tandraden."), now quoted in the evidence. | fixed |
| vomer | "Lower part of the nasal septum" is loose: the vomer forms the lower back part; the front of the septum is cartilage. | Verified against NLM's MeSH scope note for D055172 ("The vomer forms the posterior and inferior border of the NASAL SEPTUM."), added as evidence. Note changed to en "Lower back part of the nasal septum.", sv "Nedre, bakre delen av nässkiljeväggen." | fixed |
| lunate-bone | "in the middle of the first row" does not say which end the rows are counted from, and the proximal row has four bones with the pisiform. | Note changed to en "Wrist, in the row nearest the forearm, next to the scaphoid.", sv "Handloven, i raden närmast underarmen, bredvid båtbenet.", supported by sv.wikipedia Handlov (proximal row; it "ledar uppåt (proximalt) mot underarmens (antebrachium) ben"), the Svensk MeSH scope note ("beläget mellan båtbenet och os triquetrum") and en.wikipedia Lunate bone, now quoted in the evidence. | fixed |
| hamate-bone | "second row" / "andra raden" has the same counting problem as the lunate note. | Note changed to en "Wrist, in the row nearest the fingers; it has a hook.", sv "Handloven, i raden närmast fingrarna; det har en krok.", supported by sv.wikipedia Handlov (hakbenet in the distal row, which joins the metacarpals), en.wikipedia Hamate bone ("a hook-like process ... projecting from its palmar surface") and NLM's MeSH scope note, now quoted in the evidence. | fixed |

### Round 2: Language and translation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Language and translation reviewer · **Scope:** All 54 cards in English, Swedish and Latin; title, description and keywords

No errors: language tags, Swedish names (backed by Svensk MeSH, Wikidata and sv.wikipedia), English sentence case, Latin TA98 terms and the bidirectional uniqueness all correct. Five suggestions: three applied (maxilla Swedish gender agreement, ethmoid English note, the ambiguous keyword "ben"), the definite ear-bone names kept as documented, and the Latin-identical English fronts kept.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| malleus, incus, stapes | The Swedish fronts "hammaren", "städet", "stigbygeln" are definite, unlike the other single-bone fronts; Svensk MeSH has indefinite "Hammare" and "Stigbygel". | Kept, as the reviewer recommends: the definite forms are how Swedish names the ossicles (Wikidata sv labels, sv.wikipedia Hörselben "hammaren, städet och stigbygeln", Svensk MeSH "Städet"), and the bare indefinite forms name tools (a bare "städ" reads as a blacksmith's anvil). The convention is already stated in the method (Swedish names). | no change needed |
| maxilla | Swedish note "Parigt; ..." uses a neuter adjective with the common-gender "överkäke" and breaks the deck's "one on each side" pattern. | Note rewritten in both languages so that no adjective has to agree with "överkäke" (which Svensk MeSH defines as formed by two bones): en "Two bones, one on each side; they hold the upper teeth.", sv "Två ben, ett på varje sida; i dem sitter de övre tänderna." The suggested hard-palate clause was dropped instead of kept, because no source in hand states that the maxillae form the front of the palate (en.wikipedia Hard palate names the palatine process of the maxilla and the palatine bone without saying which part); the teeth fact is in the Svensk MeSH scope notes (sv "I överkäken finns den övre tandraden.", NLM en "provides tooth sockets for the superior teeth"), now quoted in the evidence. | fixed |
| ethmoid-bone | English note says the bone separates the nasal cavity "from the brain"; the Swedish says "från hjärnhålan" (the cranial cavity). | English note changed to "Between the eye sockets; separates the nasal cavity from the cranial cavity." (en.wikipedia Ethmoid bone "separates the nasal cavity from the brain ... between the two orbits", sv.wikipedia Silben "separerar näshålan från hjärnhålan", both quoted). Swedish unchanged. | fixed |
| talus | Nine English fronts (humerus, radius, ulna, vomer, sacrum, ilium, ischium, pelvis, talus) equal the Latin back; "Ankle bone" for the talus and "Upper arm bone" for the humerus were suggested. | Rejected. "Ankle bone" is ambiguous: Wikidata gives it as an en alias of both the talus (Q13100) and the tarsal bones (Q1059724), and MeSH has "Ankle Bones" as an entry term for the tarsal bones, so the front would not have one answer. "Upper arm bone" is not a Wikidata or MeSH name of the humerus (Q162595 en aliases: "bone bone"; MeSH entry terms: none such), so it could not be checked, and "humerus" is the established English name; the humerus note already says "The upper arm". As the description says, the English front is the everyday or anatomical name, and these cards are kept for their Swedish names (Method). | rejected |
| None | The Swedish keyword "ben" is ambiguous (bone or leg). | Replaced by "skelettben", as in the deck's Swedish title. | fixed |

### Round 3: Licensing, attribution and documentation (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer · **Scope:** All 54 cards' evidence and checks; every source's licence evidence, the method, queries and licensing text

No licence errors: every licence quote matched its source, the content sources (Wikidata, Svensk MeSH, NCI SEER) allow a CC0 deck, and attribution is complete; all Wikidata 'says' and sampled TA98, MeSH, SEER and Wikipedia quotes matched. Three warnings (TA98's real role in the Latin backs; back-note facts without content-source evidence; reproducibility) and five suggestions; all applied except where noted.
